rule: Use `[error]` (not `[errors]`) for the error style tag in Breeze Rich console markup
trigger: Rich markup string using `[errors]` in any Breeze utility or command file
rationale: The Breeze Rich theme defines the tag as `error`, not `errors`; using the wrong name causes a Rich markup/style parsing error at runtime

evidence.excerpt: `[errors]` is not a valid style tag in the Breeze Rich theme

rule: Exclude Python minor versions in `requires-python` using the wildcard form `!=3.x.*`, not the bare `!=3.x`, and align the excluded version with the workspace standard
trigger: `requires-python` specifier in any `pyproject.toml` that excludes a minor version without a wildcard (e.g. `!=3.14` instead of `!=3.14.*`)
rationale: A bare `!=3.14` only excludes exactly 3.14.0; the whole 3.14.x series remains installable, contrary to intent. The workspace uses `!=3.15.*` as its standard exclusion.

evidence.excerpt: bare `!=3.14` only excludes exactly Python 3.14.0, not the whole 3.14.x series

rule: When adding a new provider base class to the registry `types.py` mapping, also add the corresponding entry to the `provider.yaml` validator's `base_class_resource_map` and its tuple of resource-type strings
trigger: A new `(resource_name, base_class_fqn)` tuple added to `dev/registry/registry_tools/types.py` without a matching entry in the provider.yaml validator
rationale: The provider.yaml validator keeps its own copy of the base-class mapping; omitting an entry lets a provider ship a subclass without declaring it and CI stays green, hiding discoverability gaps

evidence.excerpt: provider can ship a RetryPolicy subclass, forget to declare it, and CI stays green

rule: When an ADR is superseded in part by a later ADR, add a `Superseded in part by ADR NNNN` note in the Status section of the older ADR
trigger: A new ADR is merged that changes decisions from an older ADR, but the older ADR's Status section is not updated
rationale: Readers landing on a stale ADR without the supersession note will reason from the wrong artefact shape; earlier ADRs in the Airflow project (0001, 0002) set the precedent of noting supersession in Status

evidence.excerpt: Status section doesn't mention that supersession the way ADRs 0001 and 0002 do

rule: Helm tests for `airflow.tplDict`-rendered annotations must include a case with two or more annotation key/value pairs to guard against YAML line-concatenation bugs
trigger: A Helm test for a template that uses `airflow.tplDict` for annotations only asserts a single annotation key
rationale: The `airflow.tplDict` helper has a known failure mode when rendering multiple annotations (YAML line concatenation); a single-annotation test passes even when the multi-annotation path is broken

evidence.excerpt: add at least one test case that sets 2+ annotations and asserts both render correctly

rule: Helm chart template tests must cover conditional rendering with a `null`/unset value and a boundary value (e.g. `0`) in addition to the happy path
trigger: A Helm test for a conditionally rendered field (e.g. `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`) covers only the enabled/set case without testing `null`, unset, or `0`
rationale: Testing only the happy path makes it easy to break conditional Helm templating logic without the test catching it; `null/unset` and `0` are the most common regression vectors

evidence.excerpt: should also cover `null/unset` and `value = 0`; easy to break templating logic otherwise

rule: When Helm chart tests migrate a component reference from `webserver` to `apiServer`, rename the test methods and parametrize IDs to reflect the new component name
trigger: A Helm test method name or parameter ID still contains `webserver_config` after the chart has migrated the volume/config to the API server
rationale: Stale test names referring to `webserver_config` cause confusion when webserver support is removed, since the volume is now `api-server-config`

evidence.excerpt: test name still refers to 'webserver_config' even though the chart now mounts API server config

rule: In the Java/Kotlin SDK, the task `execute` method parameter that provides runtime context must be named `context` (not `client`) to match Python SDK naming
trigger: A Java or Kotlin `Task.execute()` method signature with a parameter named `client` instead of `context`
rationale: The parameter provides the same concept as `context` in Python's `BaseOperator.execute(context)`; inconsistent naming across language SDKs increases cognitive load for multi-language Airflow authors

evidence.excerpt: Why has the parameter in the task be named `client` and not `context` as we have it in Python?

rule: In the Java/Kotlin SDK, task execution errors must be reported through the structured logger (forwarded to the Airflow `--logs` channel), not via `e.printStackTrace()` to JVM stderr
trigger: `e.printStackTrace()` called in any Java/Kotlin SDK task execution path alongside a structured logger call that already captures the same exception
rationale: `e.printStackTrace()` writes to JVM stderr rather than the `--logs` channel forwarded to Airflow, so the trace never appears in the task log; the structured `logger.error` already captures the full trace

evidence.excerpt: `e.printStackTrace()` writes to JVM stderr rather than the `--logs` channel forwarded to Airflow

rule: In the Java/Kotlin SDK Airflow logger adapters, capture exception stack traces via `stackTraceToString()`, not `thrown.toString()`, and accept `Throwable?` (nullable) to honour the JDK `System.Logger` contract
trigger: A `System.Logger` or logging-bridge implementation in the Java SDK stores an exception as `thrown.toString()` or declares the parameter as non-nullable `Throwable`
rationale: Using `toString()` drops the stack trace while `--logs` channel readers expect full traces; a non-null Kotlin parameter NPEs on explicit-null callers permitted by the JDK contract

evidence.excerpt: exception stored as `thrown.toString()` drops the stack trace; other providers capture full trace

rule: In the multiplexed Airflow coordinator protocol (Java/Kotlin SDK), an undecodable or unknown-type frame must not fail all in-flight requests; scope the failure to the offending frame ID or treat unknown types as non-fatal sentinels
trigger: A `catch (Throwable)` around `readFrame()`/`decode()` in the coordinator communication loop that calls `failAllWaiters(e)` unconditionally on any decode error
rationale: Under multiplexing, one forward-incompatible or malformed frame with this pattern kills the entire coordinator connection rather than isolating the single bad exchange

evidence.excerpt: one forward-incompatible / unknown message type kills the whole coordinator connection

rule: Operator `execute_complete` callbacks (deferred/trigger pattern) must raise `AirflowException` or a subclass, not `RuntimeError` or other built-in exceptions
trigger: `raise RuntimeError(...)` inside an `execute_complete` method of an Airflow operator
rationale: Raising `RuntimeError` from a deferred callback is inconsistent with Airflow operator failure semantics and prevents uniform failure handling across operators

evidence.excerpt: Raising `RuntimeError` inconsistent with typical Airflow operator semantics; prefer `AirflowException`
